doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Playing at the St. Mark's Center benefit after Toni Morrison
summary: Evacuated to Georgia and New Jersey, he plays a gig for poets and writers in the East Village that feels like a New Orleans church.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: my grandson, and I played a gig the following weekend in the East Village at this St. Mark’s Center. And the feeling and the love that was in that center at St. Mark’s was I felt like I was in the church in New Orleans because it was more a thing of poets and writers who came together to pay homage to New Orleans and Katrina and their words just portrayed how they felt about it. Some were angry about it. Some were beautiful, just peaceful. I performed after Toni Morrison, the great writer. And man she is one of my heroes in life. I love to listen to her speak. I love to listen to her speak just as much as I used to like to listen to John Coltrane or Miles Davis play. What she does with the words is what the other musicians did with the music. So I performed right after she spoke and it was so inspiring and she was very calm and beautifully articulate. There were other writers there who were very angry and militant about things and I understand that’s the way they felt. That’s the way you play music sometimes, according to how you feel. But the love that was in St. Mark’s that particular day, I was thinking, I said wow, this feels like being at home at one of those churches. And it was great. It wasn’t the same but it was very close because it was genuine and there was a lot of love right there you know.
Did it affect the way you performed that day do you think?

Oh yes it did. Because what had happened to New Orleans, it was happening to me even though I wasn’t there, looking at all the footage of all the people on the bridges and the Superdome and everything, yeah, that had a big effect on me.
